ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type

facts.raw_span: painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis of 1 month's duration
elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior
fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite
asymptomatic 'green-yellow welts' and swelling of the glans penis
swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days
no improvement with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin
glans penis and corona were grossly edematous
3.7 × 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue
no urethral discharge was present
routine blood test results were within normal limits
dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes, which were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, within the background of a reactive T-cell infiltrate
clonal IgH gene rearrangement

concepts.why: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes with specific immunophenotypic markers (CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+) and a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, along with a large and painful ulcer on the penis, supports this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
concepts.why: Although less common on the penis, the specific immunophenotypic markers and the presence of a clonal IgH gene rearrangement could also suggest this subtype of lymphoma, which typically presents with leg involvement but can occur in other sites.

concepts.preferred_label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type
concepts.why: The presence of a destructive ulcer and the specific immunophenotypic markers of the lymphocytes, although not perfectly matching, could also suggest this aggressive type of lymphoma, which can present in extranodal sites.

The clonal IgH gene rearrangement and the presence of atypical lymphocytes could also be seen in mantle cell lymphoma, although the specific markers (CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+) and the clinical presentation are not as typical for this diagnosis.

The presence of atypical lymphocytes and a clonal IgH gene rearrangement could suggest follicular lymphoma, although the clinical presentation and specific markers are less typical for this diagnosis.

rationales.F01: The presence of painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis is more typical of Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F02: Elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy discovered 9 years prior may indicate a history of lymphoma.
rationales.F06: The lack of improvement with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin suggests a non-infectious etiology.
rationales.F08: The presence of a tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue is more typical of Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F11: The dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes, which were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, within the background of a reactive T-cell infiltrate is diagnostic of B-cell lymphoma.
rationales.F12: The clonal IgH gene rearrangement is diagnostic of B-cell lymphoma.

frontier_selector.runner_up: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type
frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, strongly supports the diagnosis of a B-cell lymphoma. The clinical presentation and the lack of specific evidence against it make Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma the most fitting diagnosis.
